title: Legume-based cover cropping
intervention: Introduce legume-based cover crops (e.g., cowpea, clover, Sesbania) in rotation or intercropped with the main crop.
mechanism: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen via rhizobial symbiosis and add root biomass and leaf litter, which raises soil organic carbon and feeds soil microbial communities. Higher microbial biomass increases nutrient cycling and supports a wider range of soil fauna, which underpins aboveground biodiversity.
expected_impact: Soil organic carbon increases by approximately 15-25% over 2-3 years under continuous cover cropping.
source: FAO Soils Portal - Soil Organic Carbon; FAO (2017) 'Soil Organic Carbon: the hidden potential'

title: Agroforestry / intercropping transition
intervention: Convert monoculture plots to agroforestry or intercropping systems using regionally-appropriate tree and shrub species alongside the existing crop.
mechanism: Tree canopy reduces surface soil temperature and evapotranspiration, improving effective water-use efficiency under low rainfall. Deep root systems recycle nutrients from lower soil horizons, and structural complexity (canopy + understory + crop layer) creates additional habitat niches, directly increasing habitat diversity and species richness.
expected_impact: Agroforestry systems typically raise soil organic carbon by 10-30% over 5 years and can increase on-farm species richness by 2-4x versus monoculture, per IPCC AFOLU chapter estimates.
source: IPCC AR6 WG3 Chapter 7 (AFOLU); FAO Agroforestry guidelines

title: Native riparian buffer restoration
intervention: Re-establish native vegetation buffers of 10-30m along waterways and field edges using locally sourced species.
mechanism: Riparian buffers intercept sediment and agrochemical runoff before it reaches waterways, reducing pollution load on aquatic biodiversity. They also act as habitat corridors, reconnecting fragmented patches and reducing edge effects from adjacent land use.
expected_impact: Well-established riparian buffers reduce sediment runoff by 50-80% and nutrient (N/P) runoff by 30-60%, substantially improving downstream aquatic species survival.
source: FAO Forestry Paper 172 - Riparian buffer strips; CBD Ecosystem Restoration guidance

title: Habitat patch mosaicking (field margin diversification)
intervention: Convert a portion (5-15%) of field margins into uncultivated native wildflower/grass strips arranged as a connected mosaic rather than isolated patches.
mechanism: Connected habitat patches lower the effective isolation distance between populations, which is the dominant driver of local extinction in fragmented agricultural landscapes. Wildflower strips also provide floral resources across seasons, supporting pollinator persistence, which in turn improves crop pollination services.
expected_impact: Field margin diversification has been shown to increase local pollinator species richness by 20-45% within 2 seasons.
source: CBD Global Biodiversity Outlook; FAO Pollination Services Guidance

title: Water harvesting micro-catchments
intervention: Construct contour bunds, half-moon (demi-lune) basins, or small check dams to capture and slow surface runoff during erratic rainfall events.
mechanism: Micro-catchments increase soil moisture infiltration and reduce peak runoff velocity, buffering vegetation against both drought stress and flash-flood erosion. Stabilized soil moisture supports more consistent plant cover, which underpins herbivore and pollinator populations through the dry season.
expected_impact: Contour bunding and half-moon basins have been documented to raise plant cover by 50-300% in semi-arid rehabilitation trials within 2-3 years.
source: FAO Land and Water Division - Water harvesting techniques; IPCC AR6 WG2 (adaptation, drylands)

title: Reduced-input integrated pest management (IPM)
intervention: Shift from calendar-based synthetic pesticide application to threshold-based Integrated Pest Management using biological control agents and pest scouting.
mechanism: Broad-spectrum pesticide use suppresses non-target invertebrates that form the base of local food webs. IPM lowers total pesticide load while maintaining yield protection, allowing natural predator populations (which regulate pests) to recover, reducing dependency on further chemical input.
expected_impact: IPM adoption has been shown to reduce pesticide applications by 30-50% without yield loss, while measurably increasing beneficial arthropod abundance.
source: FAO Integrated Pest Management guidelines; IPBES Pollinators Assessment (2016)

title: Targeted soil pH amendment
intervention: Apply agricultural lime (for acidic soils) or gypsum/organic matter (for alkaline/sodic soils) based on a soil test, rather than blanket application.
mechanism: Extreme soil pH limits microbial enzyme activity and nutrient availability (notably P, and micronutrients), which constrains both crop growth and the diversity of soil biota able to persist. Correcting pH toward the 6.0-7.5 range widens the niche space for soil organisms and improves nutrient cycling efficiency.
expected_impact: Correcting pH into optimal range typically improves nutrient use efficiency by 20-40%, indirectly supporting higher microbial biomass.
source: FAO Soils Portal - Soil pH management

title: Rotational multi-species grazing
intervention: Replace continuous single-species grazing with rotational, multi-paddock grazing using mixed livestock species and rest periods.
mechanism: Rest periods allow vegetation structural recovery, creating a mosaic of sward heights that supports different invertebrate and ground-nesting bird guilds. Mixed grazing pressure (rather than continuous single-species pressure) prevents selective overgrazing of palatable species, maintaining plant community diversity.
expected_impact: Rotational grazing systems have shown 15-30% higher plant species diversity compared to continuously grazed systems within 3-5 years.
source: FAO Grassland and pasture management guidance

title: Mulching with crop residue retention
intervention: Retain and apply crop residue as surface mulch instead of removing or burning it, combined with minimum tillage.
mechanism: Surface mulch reduces direct soil evaporation and moderates soil surface temperature, conserving moisture under low-rainfall conditions. Reduced tillage preserves soil aggregate structure and fungal networks, allowing organic carbon to accumulate rather than oxidize rapidly.
expected_impact: Residue retention with minimum tillage can reduce evaporative soil moisture loss by 20-35% and raise topsoil organic carbon measurably within 3 years.

title: Ecological corridor establishment
intervention: Plant linear native vegetation corridors connecting isolated habitat fragments across the landholding or between neighboring farms.
mechanism: Corridors reduce the effective isolation distance between fragmented populations, enabling gene flow and recolonization after local extinction events, which is the central mechanism by which fragmentation reduces regional biodiversity (metapopulation theory).
expected_impact: Corridor connectivity has been associated with 25-60% higher species persistence in fragmented landscape studies over 5-10 years.
source: CBD Ecosystem Restoration guidance; IPBES Global Assessment (2019)
